intro.title: Welcome to Sefrou — cherries and cascades
intro.p1: Sefrou sits in the foothills of the Middle Atlas, about 30–40 minutes from Fez. It is a compact town known for its medina, nearby waterfalls, cherry orchards and a historic Jewish heritage that still shapes local memory and crafts.
intro.p2: Many travellers use Sefrou as a half-day or overnight from Fez: walk the medina, visit the cascades and, in season, taste the cherries that give the town its festival fame. It is quieter than the imperial cities and easy to combine with a Fez base.

medina.title: Medina of Sefrou
medina.p1: Sefrou's medina is compact and walkable — lanes, small souks and a slower pace than Fez. It is the heart of everyday town life rather than a long sightseeing circuit.
medina.p2: Go in the morning for softer light and open workshops. Dress modestly and ask before close-up photos of people.
medina.tip: Combine with a café stop before heading to the cascades.

cascades.title: Cascades de Sefrou
cascades.p1: The waterfalls near Sefrou are a short outing from the centre — green paths, water and a cool break from the plains heat in warmer months.
cascades.p2: Wear sturdy shoes; paths can be damp. Bring water and check local advice after heavy rain.
cascades.tip: Best in spring when water flow is stronger and the surrounding greenery is fresh.

cherries.title: Cherry orchards & festival
cherries.p1: Sefrou is famous for its cherries. Late spring brings the Festival des Cerises — music, parade and local produce — and orchards around the town fill with fruit.
cherries.p2: Outside festival dates you can still see orchards and buy fruit in season from markets and roadside stalls.
cherries.tip: Confirm festival dates the year you travel; they usually fall around late May or June.

souk.title: Souk & local crafts
souk.p1: Sefrou's souk brings produce, livestock and local trade on market days — practical rather than a polished tourist bazaar.
souk.p2: Confirm the market day when you arrive. Go early and keep valuables secure in crowds.
souk.tip: Good for tasting seasonal fruit and seeing everyday foothill life.

heritage.title: Jewish heritage & mellah
heritage.p1: Sefrou had a significant Jewish community for centuries. The historic mellah and related sites remain part of the town's story, even as demographics have changed.
heritage.p2: Visit with respect: this is living memory and local history, not a theme park. A local guide can add context if available.
heritage.tip: Pair with the medina walk the same morning.

fez_link.title: Road from Fez
fez_link.p1: Fez is about 30–40 minutes by road. Sefrou works well as a half-day trip from a Fez base or as a quiet overnight if you want foothill air.
fez_link.p2: Grands taxis and shared transport serve the route; a private driver or rental car gives more flexibility for the cascades.
fez_link.tip: Leave Fez early to enjoy the medina and waterfalls before afternoon heat.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Sefrou?
q1.answer: A half-day covers the medina and cascades; one night if you want a quieter foothill base near Fez.

q2.question: When is the cherry festival?
q2.answer: Usually late May or June. Confirm exact dates for the year you travel.

q3.question: How do I get to Sefrou from Fez?
q3.answer: About 30–40 minutes by grand taxi, bus or car. Easy as a half-day trip from a Fez hotel.

q4.question: Are the cascades easy to reach?
q4.answer: Yes — a short taxi or drive from the centre. Wear sturdy shoes; paths can be damp.

itinerary.title: Suggested 2–3 Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A balanced plan for the medina, cascades and cherry country without rushing.

detailed_itinerary.day3_tab: Day 3 — Fez Link or Free Time
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Walk the compact medina while it is calm. Note workshops, small souks and the everyday pace of the foothill town.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Head to the waterfalls for green paths and a cool break. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Simple grill or café in the centre — early night if you stay over.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: In season, visit cherry orchards or festival events if dates match. Outside season, a quiet market morning still shows local produce.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Explore the historic mellah and Jewish heritage sites with respect, then return to the medina lanes.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Taste local fruit in season and a simple tagine before resting.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Another waterfall walk if the light is good, or the weekly souk if it falls on your day.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Drive or taxi back to Fez for the imperial medina, or continue toward Azrou and Ifrane if your route heads into the Middle Atlas.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Dinner in Fez or a simple stop on the road — close a short Sefrou chapter.
